A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PQN research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–E are available and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated appendix content.

before.justification: v3 reports original PQN experiments, including Baird’s counterexample, Atari, Craftax and multi-agent evaluations, with additional empirical results in Appendix D.

after.justification: v6 retains original PQN training results, benchmark comparisons and ablations in Section 5 and Appendix D.

M1.justification: The regularised Q-network, parallel sampling, recursive λ-return targets and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged, as do the RNN and multi-agent adaptations.

E1.justification: Both retain Baird’s counterexample, DeepSea, classic control, MinAtar, Atari, Craftax, SMAX, Overcooked and Hanabi. Removing detailed MinAtar ablation plots does not remove its games from evaluation.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is retained. In particular, v3 Figure 16 and v6 Figure 14 both show PQN, CrossQ, PQN with BatchNorm and PPO; CrossQ is not a newly added baseline.

E3.justification: The stated budgets, evaluation procedures, architectures and hyperparameters in Appendices C and E are unchanged. Figure 10 retains the same controlled MinAtar parallelisation comparison. Revised plots do not document a protocol change.

E4.justification: v6 removes v3 Figures 11–12, which disaggregate the parallel-environment ablation into sample- and time-efficiency curves for four MinAtar games. Aggregate evidence remains in Figures 6e and 10, so this reduces diagnostic detail without removing the overall analysis.

E5.justification: Both state that results use 10 seeds, except ALE results using 3 seeds, and retain shaded uncertainty displays. No change to the stated statistical estimation or uncertainty-reporting procedure is introduced.

E6.justification: The per-game MinAtar ablation result entries disappear. Displayed traces and bands also change in the redrawn Atari-10 figure and the Craftax replay-buffer panel, without an explanation establishing reruns. Headline numerical tables remain unchanged, including Table 3’s PQN 400M-frame median of 245 and 40 above-human games.

T1.justification: The assumptions, stability theorems, proofs and λ-return derivation are retained. Policy/distribution notation and the description of the optimal-policy set are clarified; Appendix B.4 adds attribution without changing its mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: stability through LayerNorm and regularisation, and efficient parallel Q-learning without target networks or a large replay buffer.

C2.justification: Interpretations and qualifications remain unchanged, including regularisation’s effect on fixed points, difficult exploration games, and reduced sample efficiency under the alternative sticky-action ALE configuration.

D1.justification: The code-access information, hardware specifications, RAdam implementation details, network descriptions and Appendix E hyperparameter values are retained.

R1.justification: Appendix B.4 newly identifies Daley and Amato (2019, Appendix D) as the original source of the repeated and adapted λ-return derivation. That work was already cited elsewhere; the broader related-work discussion is unchanged.

P1.justification: Edits are limited to notation and wording corrections, the attribution sentence in Appendix B.4, and updated figure references. The section structure and substantive narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Two MinAtar figures are removed. The Atari-10 raster-panel collection becomes a consolidated vector figure with reordered panels and a shared legend. Other appendix figures and hyperparameter tables are repositioned, with limited additional plot-formatting changes.

improvement.justification: Explicit attribution in Appendix B.4 and a more readable Atari-10 figure improve clarity. However, v6 removes per-game MinAtar diagnostic evidence and changes some appendix curve traces without explaining the revisions. With the main theory, protocols and headline findings retained, these mixed effects do not establish a reliable net improvement or deterioration.
